text: So, many people think that Nifty gives
amazing returns if you let compounding
happen, but they miss a very critical
point. Take a look at this chart and you
can divide this chart into two spheres.
The first period starts from 1999. Here,
Nifty went from 1,000 all the way all
the way till 6,000, right? So, I will
just write it here, 6,000, 6 X returns.
But between this point and this point,
Nifty only went 4.2 X. So, it took Nifty
to go from 1,000 all the way till 6,000
in a matter of 10 years, but for the
next 16-17 years, it only went 4 X, 4.5
X. Now, the important message here is
that people look at Nifty returns in
entirety. They look at that, "Hey, Nifty
went from this point A to point B and
ended up giving 26 X or 26 buying
returns in 26 years." So, therefore, if
we start investing in Nifty 50 starting
in the year 2026, we will end up with
amazing gains. Is this really true? No.
So, for this, you need to again go back
and understand what is happening in this
phase. This entire phase was the
adoption phase of the India's stock
market. Our stock market was really
small. It was unproven. There were
opportunities to make money. It was
extremely difficult to invest in the
Indian stock market. If you have
grandfather, father, or grandmother who
used to invest in Indian stocks back in
the '90s, go and ask them
>> [music]
>> how easy was it for them to go and place
a buy order on a particular stock. It
was incredibly tough. But now, things
have simplified. Everyone assumes
sitting here in 2026 that, "You know
what? If we continue to run our SIPs, we
will end up making crazy gains.
We if we just go on Zerodha and continue
to buy stocks or Groww and continue to
buy stocks, we'll somehow become
multi-millionaires." Is that really
true? I don't know, right? But this is
an important point for you to go ahead
and investigate that, "Hey, majority of
the gains that came on Nifty 50 came in
the first decade. Since then our markets
haven't done amazingly well and even
prominent fund managers like Parag
Parikh Flexi Cap Fund, right? They are
talking about the fact that our markets
might not give amazing returns. So what
is it that you need to focus on? This is
